name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 4
aliases: Mitochondrial Combined Respiratory Chain Deficiency Type 4

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of combined defects in multiple mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of multisystem clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial disease including neurological and muscular symptoms
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear or mitochondrial genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of combined biochemical defects in respiratory chain complexes plus compatible clinical features and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, histological, and genetic data.

searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

common.notes: Generalized decreased muscle tone and strength
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Elevated lactate levels due to impaired oxidative metabolism
Various seizure types including focal and generalized

rare.notes: Secondary to mitochondrial dysfunction in pancreatic cells

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and muscle atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial assembly factors or mitochondrial DNA maintenance genes
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers
Abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Prominent lactic acidosis with episodic neurological deterioration
Isolated optic neuropathy without multisystem involvement
Typically adolescent or young adult onset

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in infancy or early childhood
Multisystem involvement including neurological, muscular, and cardiac symptoms
Elevated lactate levels with combined respiratory chain enzyme deficiencies
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
